world.title: Reforms Transformed Media, Says Ethiopian Media Authority Director-General
world.description:
Addis Ababa, August 16, 2026 (ENA) —Ethiopian Media Authority Director-General Haimanot Zeleke said recent reforms have transformed the media by removing licensing bottlenecks, expanding access and content diversity, coupling greater freedom with stronger professional responsibility and capacity-building.
Ethiopia’s media landscape has been significantly reshaped by the reforms, she added.
In an interview with the ENA, the Director-General noted that the changes have enabled media institutions to expand in type, number, accessibility and content, creating a more open and competitive environment for information flow between the public and the government.
“By reforming previous licensing bottlenecks in the media sector, opportunities have been created for numerous professionals and institutions wishing to enter the field,” Haimanot said, adding that this has directly increased participation and diversified content.
According to her, revising preconditions that once constrained the profession has allowed media workers to operate more freely, while stressing that “media freedom must go hand-in-hand with professional responsibility and respect for the law.”
The Authority has also paired this liberalization with efforts to raise standards. She highlighted that training delivered through the Ethiopian Media Excellence Center have graduated selected journalists from various outlets to cultivate reporters who work effectively, inform the public, and bring agendas closer to the people.
The Director-General said capacity-building and content monitoring are being used not only to grow the sector in quantity and reach but also to enhance professional competence and the quality of information provided to citizens.
Addressing digital-era challenges, Haimanot stated that the Authority is working with relevant bodies to curb the spread of false information and hate speech.
Looking ahead, she pledged actions to further strengthen the media landscape and support democratic system-building.
“Support will be provided to ensure healthy media institutions grow further and operate in line with professional ethics and legal principles,” she said, adding that the Authority will educate, train and bring into the legal framework those outlets and professionals not operating along proper professional lines.
The Director-General concluded that ongoing capacity-building aims to ensure media outlets serve as reliable bridges between the public and government, enabling citizens to access accurate information, report issues freely and professionally, and play a constructive role on national matters.

science.title: Evaluating the role of some selected herbal extracts as biostimulant for mitigating drought and heat stress in wheat crop
science.description: Emerging incidence of drought and heat stress are the major constrains for wheat production. Identifying natural and sustainable methods of crop protection are required to deal global climate change and environmental degradation. In view of our objective, the aim of the present study was designed to test four herbal plant extracts; Phyllanthus emblica, Plumbago zeylanica, Bacopa monnieri and Curcuma longa, as biostimulant to improve drought and heat stress tolerance in wheat crop. The effects of these extracts were assessed through morphological and biochemical parameters. The results indicated an increase in the tested parameters by all the herbal treatments, with P. emblica being the most effective one, causing around 1.4–2.4 fold increase in plant length, leaf biomass and seed biomass, whereas 2.0-2.6 fold increase in pigments, total phenolics, flavonoid, antioxidant activity and enzyme activity. Morphology-based stress tolerance index (STI) of 1.28–0.83 for the treatment as compared to 0.48–0.65 of control revealed significantly higher maintenance of growth and biomass in biostimulant treated plants. Composite performance index (CPI), integrating physiological and biochemical traits, demonstrated a coordinated enhancement of antioxidant defense and metabolic stability with values of 0.89 and 0.82 for treated plants as compared to 0.42 − 0.37 of control. Heat map visualization and principal component analysis (PCA) further confirmed clear discrimination between control and treated samples, identifying the role of herbal extract in stress resilience. We performed UHPLC-HRMS analysis to identify possible biostimulant in the natural extracts. A range of phytohormones involved in stress tolerance, such as salicylic acid, auxins and gibberellic acid were detected in the sample indicating their role in stress mitigation. The outcome of the research work will help in developing natural and sustainable methods of crop protection and will promote the usage of herbal biostimulant in crop fields.

science.title: Dynamic heterogeneous graph-structured knowledge tracing with multi-behavior integration and temporal forgetting
science.description: Knowledge tracing (KT) aims to estimate the temporal evolution of learners’ knowledge states and predict future exercise performance. Most existing KT methods focus on exercise-response sequences and therefore cannot explicitly distinguish knowledge exposure through learning resources from knowledge verification through problem solving. We propose Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph-Structured Knowledge Tracing (DHGKT), a framework that organizes learners, exercises, videos, concepts, and optional comments within a unified relational event representation. Each learner is associated with an interpretable concept-mastery vector. Before each event, an exponential temporal decay is applied; video events provide a duration-aware exposure signal, whereas exercise events calibrate the state through prediction-error feedback. Semantic concept-video weighting and concept-aligned social exposure are treated as auxiliary extensions rather than indispensable components. Under a chronological 70%/10%/20% training/validation/test split with five random seeds on four MOOCCubeX courses, DHGKT-Core achieved an average test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.8529, compared with 0.8318 for its exercise-only variant and 0.7508 for a same-input multi-behavior fusion control. The contribution of video behavior was course dependent: it improved three courses but reduced performance on C_801420. Fixed and learnable topology-aggregation variants produced negligible AUC changes, and the semantic and social extensions did not yield reliable additional gains. These results indicate that the principal value of DHGKT lies in transparent event-driven knowledge-state evolution rather than generic graph convolution. The revision further clarifies the roles of behavioral modalities, graph-event semantics, decay sensitivity, and evaluation limitations in response to the second-round comments.

science.title: Specific targeting of cancer cell mitochondria with a malaria drug improves pancreatic cancer outcome
science.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal malignancy. In this paper, we present DZ-ART1, a first-in-class, dual-function therapeutic. This innovative agent is composed of a tumor-targeting heptamethine carbocyanine dye conjugated to artemisinin (ART). Near-infrared imaging demonstrated precise tumor localization of DZ-ART1 in mice. DZ-ART1 accumulated 5- to 10-fold more in cancer cells compared to normal cells. DZ-ART1 significantly decreased the survival of eight PDAC cell lines with little effect on normal cells. It increased the lethal effect of chemotherapies in vitro and in vivo. Functional assays confirmed DZ-ART1’s ability to disrupt mitochondrial bioenergetics, deplete ATP, and induce reactive oxygen species production. Mitochondrial depletion of cancer cells decreased DZ-ART1 uptake and cytotoxicity, highlighting its mechanistically unique, mitochondria-dependent action. Transcriptomic profiling revealed DZ-ART1’s broad reprogramming of PDAC pathways related to cell survival, cancer stemness, and metastasis. In three rigorously validated preclinical models — Krasþ/LSLG12D;Trp53þ/LSLR172H;Pdx-1-Cre (KPC) transgenic, syngeneic, and patient-derived xenografts (PDX) — DZ-ART1 markedly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis and prolonged survival, all without toxicity to normal tissues. DZ-ART1 represents a new class of anti-cancer therapeutics that uniquely combines diagnostic imaging and cancer cell organelle-specific targeting.
